How Creative Maps Make Air Pollution More Visible

2026-07-03 The Conversation air pollution mapping, citizen science, York air map, bicycle monitoring, air quality visualization, creative data mapping, environmental data, pollution exposure, public health
Read the source article

Quick summary

Researchers at the University of York combined bicycle-mounted air quality sensors, citizen science, and creative visualization to create the York Air Map — revealing how pollution exposure varies dramatically over just a few meters and making invisible environmental data tangible for the public.

Key takeaways

  • 16 small air quality monitors attached to bicycles collected data during daily cycling commutes across York over six-week blocks
  • Citizen scientists could see pollution data change in real-time through sensors and phone apps, connecting statistics to lived experience
  • Air pollution exposure is not evenly distributed — fluctuations can occur within short distances depending on traffic, road works, park proximity, and construction
  • The York Air Map translates complex environmental data into accessible maps, visualizations, a zine, public exhibitions, and community workshops
  • One exhibition featured smellable air filters exposed to different pollution sources, letting visitors guess sources like wood burning, BBQs, and household products
  • Pollution diaries showed that citizen scientists became more attuned to their surroundings over time, noticing smells and sources when spikes appeared
  • Fixed monitoring stations provide accurate data but only at limited points; mobile citizen science fills spatial gaps
